# Engine runtime: loop, clock, commands, snapshots

## Purpose

<!-- hand:purpose -->
> Draft — owner review pending.

The engine runtime: the fixed-step clock, the committed pipeline state and its look-ahead, the sample ring buffers, the
seeded random streams and snapshots. It decides when and in which order each model is advanced, and makes a run
reproducible: the same seed and command log give the same patient. It matters mostly to an embedding developer; a
clinician-educator needs only that time moves in 20 ms ticks and can run from 0.25 to 8 times real time.
<!-- /hand:purpose -->

## Equations in words

<!-- hand:equations -->
> Draft — owner review pending.

- Clock: simT = tick × 20 ms; wall time feeds an accumulator, acc += min(wall Δ, 250 ms) × timeScale, and a tick runs
  while acc ≥ 20 ms; timeScale is limited to 0.25–8 ("Fix Your Timestep", Gaffer on Games; `clock/clock.ts`).
- The ECG runs at 500 Hz, 10 samples per tick (`engine.ts`); ring buffers are indexed by absolute sample number, sample
  n belonging to time n/rate, and keep the most recent 120 s (`buffers/ring.ts`).
- Look-ahead: every tick a clone of the committed state is run 100 ms ahead to fill the buffers and find QRS detections
  early enough to schedule beeps; a command invalidates everything after "now", and tones whose detection vanished are
  revoked by id (`engine.ts`).
- Order within a tick: queued commands due at that tick are applied, the ECG and QRS detector run, then the drug model
  first so every consumer reads this instant's effects (`engine.ts`); the neuro model follows the drug model and comes
  before the respiratory pipeline (`l2/neuro/pipeline.ts`), and the endocrine step comes after the blood
  (`l2/endo/pipeline.ts`); the device layer and the truth event close the tick (`engine.ts`).
- Randomness: one sfc32 stream per subsystem, each seeded from hash(seed, name) with cyrb53, so drawing from one stream
  never shifts another (`rng/sfc32.ts`; NOTICES N-006).
- Snapshots: all pipeline state is plain JSON-safe data; NaN, ± Infinity, −0 and undefined travel as tagged objects so a
  restored snapshot is the same patient (`snapshot-codec.ts`).
<!-- /hand:equations -->

### [`engine.ts`](../../packages/engine-core/src/engine.ts)

| Name | Value | Unit | Source / tag | Comment |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `BUFFER_SECONDS` | `120` | — | brief §3.5 | brief §3.5 |
| `BEEP_DELAY_S` | `0.03` | s | — | Tone at detected R + 30 ms. |
| `REST_AVG_S` | `20` | s | brief §4.3; research/45; [ENG procedure: REST_AVG_S, five spontaneous breaths at the default 15/min; REST_SEED, the engine's default seed.] | SV₀, the reference of the pleth's PI × SVᵢ/SV₀ rule (brief §4.3), is the patient's OWN settled resting stroke volume: what this engine reaches for this patient at rest — spontaneously breathing, unventilated, in sinus rhythm — once its own stabilisation (the MANUAL trackers, or MODELED's reflexes) has run. It is MEASURED here by running the real engine on that resting patient, not typed and not taken from the stand-alone stabiliser, so the pulse equals the instructor's PI exactly at that rest and departs from it only as the stroke volume departs from it. Why the stand-alone stabiliser's `circ.ref.sv` (79.1 mL for the default adult) is not that value — the running engine settles the same MANUAL patient at ≈ 89 mL (brief 76, research/45; measured below): `stabilise.ts` solves the bare circuit for the PROFILE's targets (HR 70, CVP 5, the band's SBP/DBP) at a CONSTANT end-expiratory pleural pressure (P_PL0 −4 mmHg). Three couplings of the running engine are missing from it: 1. MANUAL: the instructor's own numbers (L1 defaults HR 75, CVP 6, 120/80), which the MANUAL trackers then impose with THEIR knobs — the venous unstressed volume (≈ −400 mL) and LV Emax (×0.74) — not the stabiliser's (R_sys, C_art). Measured at seed 42, 45–90 s: HR 75/CVP 6 → 88 mL; HR 70/CVP 4.85 (the stabiliser's own targets) → 86 mL. 2. The breath driver: spontaneous breathing swings the pleural pressure from −4 to ≈ −7 mmHg (mean ≈ −5), which raises venous return, and the MANUAL CVP tracker holds the breath-AVERAGED right-atrial pressure, so it fills by a further ≈ 130 mL to lift the inspiratory dips (that residual 86 against 79 mL). 3. MODELED: the same breathing, and the baroreflex settling at its own point (81.2 mL at rest: SV₀; 70.8 mL on IPPV). The same fault — the trackers starting from a circulation that is not the instructor's patient and taking ≈ 40–60 s to reach it — is behind the MANUAL PEEP 0 < PEEP 5 stroke volume (84.0 against 85.5 mL): a ventilator started at t = 0 runs while the trackers are still converging. Under PEEP 5 the pressure tracker kept running to 38 s (LV Emax ×0.80) and the volume tracker, which subtracts the pleural RISE from its CVP, transfused 665 mL; under PEEP 0 the pressure tracker released at ≈ 10 s (Emax ×1.00, SBP then drifting to 129) and the volume tracker gave 367 mL. The order PEEP 0 < PEEP 5 is that race, not physiology; it is left to the trackers' own brief (no waveform here changes). The rest is the patient as configured at t = 0 (profile, conditions and the instructor's baseline values) with its scripted arrhythmia removed: a rhythm and its rate are the scenario's (the AF pulse deficit must show against the patient's sinus stroke volume, research/45), so a non-sinus `rhythm` drops with its `baseline.hr`, and the monitor's `sensors` drop too. The settling ends when both MANUAL trackers have released (each releases by MANUAL_TRACK_MAX_S of its own run), or after REST_SETTLE_MODELED_S in MODELED; SV₀ is then the mean pleth stroke-volume estimate (EDV − the previous beat's ESV, the numerator the pleth uses) over REST_AVG_S of beats. A patient property, not the scenario's random stream: the run uses REST_SEED, so it is deterministic and cached per resting patient and mode, and it runs ONCE, when the engine is created — never inside a step, whatever the time scale. The run steps only the three pipelines that set a resting stroke volume (`restAdvance`: the rhythm engine, the breath driver, the haemodynamics), tick by tick as the engine does; it reproduces the whole engine's resting value exactly (88.90 / 81.29 mL, MANUAL / MODELED, at a 60 s MODELED settle) at ≈ 60 % of its cost. The resting patient carries no sensors (their transducers are not physiology: SV₀ is the same with or without them) and MODELED settles REST_SETTLE_MODELED_S, so a run is ≈ 0.1–0.2 s in Node and Chromium; the whole engine's 80 s took 0.23–0.29 s and, on the CI runner, delayed a case's monitor by 1–2 s. A restored snapshot carries its own SV₀. [ENG procedure: REST_AVG_S, five spontaneous breaths at the default 15/min; REST_SEED, the engine's default seed.] |
| `REST_SEED` | `1` | — | — | — |
| `REST_SETTLE_MODELED_S` | `20` | s | — | MODELED has no tracker to wait for: its resting SV is within ± 0.5 % (the breath-to-breath spread) from 16 s on. |
